title: Optimize Field Kit — SDR Technical Play & Slide Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick field kit for SDRs and technical AE partners to introduce Redwood Optimize (cost/perf toolkit) in discovery and executive conversations. Not a product spec — sales-facing slides + speaker notes + rapid objection handling.

Slide 1 — Title: Redwood Optimize — Cut inference unit cost while preserving quality
- One-line opener: Reduce per-token spend up to 3x through batching, cache, and model selection.
- Speaker note: Use a customer example up front — e.g., '14M monthly tokens, moved from naive p50 to cache-aware routing; net spend -47% in month 1.' Keep to 20s.

Slide 2 — Why Optimize matters now
- LLMs iterate fast: doubling context/seq lengths and larger model variants increase op costs
- Customers ramp quickly (pilot -> prod) and cost surprises kill adoption
- Optimize provides prescriptive config + automated suggestions to keep unit economics stable
- Note: emphasize predictable ROI, not just raw savings.

Slide 3 — Core levers (one-liners)
- Batching policies: latency-aware batching for bursty workloads
- KV/prefix caching: eliminate repeated token compute for common prompts
- Quantization profiles: maintain quality with INT8/INT4 where appropriate
- Routing policies: route by latency vs cost across model variants
- Speaker note: have 1-sentence explanation of each for non-technical execs.

Slide 4 — Typical customer play (SMB -> Midmarket example)
- Phase 1 (pilot): hosted API + default optimize suggestions; 10–15% cost savings immediate
- Phase 2 (scale): enable batch and cache on per-route basis, model variant rollouts; 30–50%
- Phase 3 (commit): Dedicated + optimized quantization + routing = predictable unit economics
- Customer story snippet: 'FinAssist reduced inference bill by 39% and improved 95th-latency by 12ms.'

Slide 5 — Demo checklist for calls (tech AE/SDR joint)
- Ask about prompt shapes: repeated system prompts? long tails?
- Traffic profile: p50/p95 token lengths, steady vs spiky patterns
- SLOs: latency targets, acceptable p95 degradation
- Current stack: self-hosted? cloud endpoints? any existing caching?
- Quick win suggestions to mention live: enable KV-cache on templates; try mini-batching for background jobs.

Slide 6 — Rebuttals & talking points (procurement/finance)
- "We can just use cheaper GPUs": Explain software-side levers matter — batching and caching reduce GPU hours more effectively than swapping hardware in the short term.
- "Quantization will break things": Present the evaluation framework: A/B on a holdout eval set with rollback and automatic quality alerts.
- "Migration to Dedicated is expensive": Frame committed capacity vs unpredictable cloud egress and overprovisioning; show a 12-month TCO scenario.

Slide 7 — Quick math (scripts for SDRs)
- Use this simple formula on calls: estimated_monthly_tokens * current_cost_per_token * (1 - expected_savings_pct) = projected_spend
- Script example: 'If you're at $X/k tokens, most customers see 20–40% with basic Optimize settings — will you want us to run a quick ROI estimate together?'

Slide 8 — Objection: "We don't want vendor-controlled config"
- Response: Optimize provides recommended configs; customer can approve, pin, or opt-out per-route. Clear audit logs + RBAC.

Slide 9 — Walkthrough: Live pilot proposal (15–30 days)
- Kickoff: define key routes (2–3) and eval prompts
- Instrumentation: enable token-level tracing + baseline run (48h)
- Run: auto-suggest batching/cache + 1 A/B eval over 7–14 days
- Deliverable: savings estimate, latency impact, rollout plan
- Costs: minimal setup time, recommend customer-owned tokens for private evals

Slide 10 — Appendix: Example snippets to share in follow-up email
- Short one-liner: 'We run a lightweight pilot across 2 routes: estimate savings in 10 business days — no infra changes required.'
- 3 bullets for execs: Cost predictability, Audit & compliance, Path to dedicated capacity
- Links: Confluence pilot checklist, demo notebook, previous ROI case study PDF

Speaker notes + TODOs (internal):
- TODO: convert the math slide into an interactive spreadsheet for AE use (JIRA-OPS-987).
- TODO: record a 6-min demo video for SDRs to include in outreach.
- Note to Samir: validate quantization SLAs with Applied ML on edge cases (long-context chat).

Unresolved questions (for PD/Applied-ML):
- We need a standard set of eval prompts to use in pilot templates — propose 6 diverse prompt archetypes.
- When can we offer a canned ROI calc in Console? current ETA unknown.

Copy for outreach emails (short):
- Subject: Quick pilot to reduce inference unit cost by ~30%
- Body (1 paragraph): 'We help engineering teams reduce per-token spend through batching, prefix caching, and smart routing. We can run a no-infra pilot across 2 routes to estimate savings in 10 business days. Interested in a quick intro?'

Appendix B — Internal quick reference table (for memorization):
- Batching: good for background jobs / bursty traffic
- Cache: great for template-heavy prompts like email gen, summaries
- Quantization: best for stable models with eval coverage
- Routing: for cost vs latency tradeoffs across model pool

End notes: keep this deck lean — one-page summary + 6 slides max for first outreach. Heavy technical deep dives belong in follow-up technical deck.
